options.text: Approve the joint break at 08:30: the two tellers started at 07:00, staff welfare keeps errors down, and the other four windows can cover for 30 minutes.
options.outcome: With 4 windows the hall serves only 48 an hour against 96 arriving, so the queue grows by 48 an hour. Staff welfare matters, but taking two windows out at the peak is the most common cause of salary-day queues.

options.text: Keep all 6 windows open, put an apology sign at the door, and ask customers to be patient; at 72 served an hour the queue should clear by midday.
options.outcome: Six windows serve 72 against 96 arriving, so the queue still grows by 24 an hour, about 48 people by 10:00. Without the greeter moving simple requests, the windows cannot keep up.

options.text: Ask every teller to aim for 4 minutes a customer instead of 5, approve one of the two breaks now, and keep the other teller until 10:00.
options.outcome: Five windows at 15 an hour serve 75, still short of 96, and pressure to rush raises errors. The fixes the course teaches are open windows at peak and moving simple requests to digital channels.

tasks.subject: My customers pay me by mobile wallet, but payments are failing
body: Ato Tolosa sells grain wholesale at the Bishoftu market. Buyers pay him into his mobile wallet, and on market days some payments fail. He has heard that wallets have limits.
His plan: open wallets in the names of his wife and two sons, and ask buyers to split their payments between them.

exhibit.title: Ato Tolosa's market-day receipts and the wallet limits

rows.label: Payments received on a busy market day
Bank A current or savings account

options.text: Open a Bank A account in his name with mobile banking, have large buyers pay into it, keep the wallet for small sales, and explain why family wallets are unsafe.
options.outcome: Right. Birr 180,000 is above both the Birr 75,000 balance limit and the Birr 150,000 daily limit, while an account has no such limits. Wallets in relatives' names put his business money in other people's control and may breach KYC rules.

options.text: Support the family plan: three wallets in his wife's and sons' names can receive up to Birr 450,000 a day, more than his busiest market day needs.
options.outcome: Splitting one business's money across relatives' wallets to get around NBE limits is unsafe and may breach KYC rules. The money legally belongs to whoever holds each wallet.

options.text: Tell him to move money out of the wallet to his supplier after every few payments, so the balance never reaches the Birr 75,000 limit.
options.outcome: Emptying the wallet helps with the balance limit, but Birr 180,000 still breaks the Birr 150,000 daily transaction limit. The real fix is to receive large payments into an account.

options.text: Advise him to ask buyers to pay in cash on market days and bring the cash to the branch each evening, where there is no limit on deposits.
options.outcome: Cash is less safe and slower for him and his buyers, and the branch loses the chance to bring a trader's flows into an account. Match the product to the need.

tasks.subject: Is the loan really 17%?
body: Weizero Hana has a Bank A offer letter for a one-year small business loan to buy salon equipment. The credit team has already approved it. She is comparing it with an offer from a friend's lender and asks you: "The letter says 17%. Is that what it costs me?"

rows.label: Interest rate
rows.value: 17% a year, paid with the principal at the end of the year

tasks.ask: How do you explain the cost?

options.text: "You receive Birr 78,000 and repay Birr 93,600: a cost of Birr 15,600, about 20% a year on what you receive. Ask the other lender for the same three numbers."
options.outcome: Correct: interest 80,000 x 17% = 13,600, fee 80,000 x 2.5% = 2,000, received 78,000, total cost 15,600, and 15,600 / 78,000 = 20.0%. Explaining in Birr and as an APR is what disclosure requires, and it lets her compare fairly.

options.text: "The rate is 17%, exactly as written in the letter. The 2.5% fee is a one-time charge at the start, so it does not change the yearly rate."
options.outcome: A fee deducted at the start raises the true cost. Leaving it out of the answer is the misunderstanding the APR exists to prevent.

options.text: "Add the fee to the rate: 17% plus 2.5% makes the true cost 19.5% a year. Compare that figure with the other lender's rate plus its fees."
options.outcome: Close, and honest in spirit, but not right. The fee is taken from the money she receives, so the cost is 15,600 on 78,000, about 20.0%. Use the Birr totals and divide by what she actually gets.

options.text: "Ours will be cheaper than an outside lender. Sign today and I will ask the manager to waive the Birr 2,000 fee, since the credit team already approved it."
options.outcome: You cannot promise a fee waiver the bank has not approved, or claim to know the other offer without seeing it. Give her the written terms, the Birr numbers and time to decide.

tasks.subject: Remittance for an elderly customer: the nephew wants the cash
body: Weizero Aster Tefera, 74, comes to collect money her son sent from Toronto. Her ID, the reference, the sender's name and the amount all match the message. Her nephew, who came with her, answers every question and asks the teller to hand the cash to him "because she cannot carry money". Weizero Aster says little.
She does not have an account at Bank A.

options.text: Speak to Weizero Aster herself, pay the Birr 75,000 to her alone, and offer her a savings account so she takes home only what she needs.
options.outcome: Right: 500 x 150.00 = Birr 75,000 at the buying rate, the rate at which the bank buys her dollars. The money goes to the named recipient, a companion who answers every question is a warning sign, and an account turns a payout into a relationship.

options.text: Pay the Birr 75,000 to the nephew after Weizero Aster nods her agreement, since she is elderly, the details all match and she cannot carry the cash.
options.outcome: A remittance is paid only to the named, identified recipient. Watch for pressure from relatives who insist on handling an elder's money.

options.text: Pay Weizero Aster Birr 76,500 in cash at today's rate of Birr 153.00, count it twice in front of her, and give her the countersigned voucher.
options.outcome: Right person, wrong rate. When the bank buys foreign currency from a customer it uses the buying rate: 500 x 150.00 = Birr 75,000. The teller's till will be Birr 1,500 short at day end.

options.text: Pay Weizero Aster Birr 75,000 in cash at the buying rate, count it twice in front of her, and give her the voucher and a polite goodbye.
options.outcome: Correct and compliant, but a missed chance to protect a vulnerable customer and win an account. Offering an account keeps most of the cash off the street.

tasks.subject: Customer wants an account without interest
body: Ato Ibrahim Yusuf, a shop owner, wants to deposit his savings but does not want to earn interest. The officer proposes opening a normal savings account and setting the interest rate on it to zero, "which is the same thing and quicker".
A second customer at the same desk, Weizero Lensa Abdi, asked for "the best savings account" and was offered only a fixed deposit.
tasks.ask: What do you tell the officer?

options.text: Open a wadiah or qard account for Ato Ibrahim as its own product, and ask Weizero Lensa about her needs before showing both options.
options.outcome: Right. Under SBB/72/2019 interest-free products are kept separate from conventional business, so they are opened as their own product types. Every customer should hear both kinds of option, based on needs, not assumptions.

options.text: Agree with the officer: a savings account with the rate set to zero gives Ato Ibrahim exactly what he wants, and it opens in half the time.
options.outcome: A conventional account with the interest removed is still a conventional product. The directive requires interest-free business to be kept separate, and the customer may not get what he believes he has.

options.text: Offer Ato Ibrahim a mudarabah account at a fixed 10% return, so he earns something on his savings while still avoiding interest.
options.outcome: A mudarabah account shares profit; its return is not guaranteed and is not a fixed rate. Promising a fixed return misstates the product.

options.text: Tell Ato Ibrahim that this branch cannot help with interest-free savings and give him the address of the nearest full interest-free bank.
options.outcome: Bank A offers interest-free products through its window. Sending a customer away for a product you have loses the deposit and the relationship.

tasks.from: Caller saying he is from the NBE
tasks.subject: "I need this customer's balance now"
body: A caller says he works in NBE supervision and needs the current balance and last month's transactions of Kaleb Furniture PLC, one of your customers, "before noon". He gives the company's account number and the owner's name correctly, and sounds impatient.

options.text: Decline politely, explain that authorities request in writing through official channels, take his details, and report the call to compliance.
options.outcome: Knowing an account number authorizes nothing, and a voice on the phone cannot be verified. Account information is shared only with the customer, a person authorized in writing, or where the law requires it, through the proper channel.

options.text: Read him the balance and last month's total: the NBE supervises Bank A, he knows the account number and owner, and he needs it before noon.
options.outcome: Right. A genuine authority sends a written request that the bank verifies and answers through its legal or compliance unit. Reporting the call helps the bank spot a social engineering attempt.

options.text: Give him only a rounded figure, "above Birr 1 million", so he can start his work, and ask him to send a formal letter for the exact numbers.
options.outcome: An approximate balance is still customer information disclosed without authorization. The compliance gate does not have a "small breach" setting.

options.text: Call him back on the mobile number he gives to confirm he is genuine, then read him the balance and transactions he asked for.
options.outcome: A number supplied by the caller proves nothing about who he is. Even a verified authority receives information through the bank's formal process, not by phone at the counter.

tasks.subject: Pensioner transferring Birr 250,000 while on the phone
body: Ato Worku Bekele, 70, asks to transfer Birr 250,000, most of his savings, to an account in another city. His phone is on speaker. A caller who says he is from "Bank A head office" tells him what to say and that the transfer will "protect his pension account from hackers". Ato Worku is anxious and wants it done quickly.

options.text: Ask him kindly to end the call, explain at a quiet desk that Bank A never asks customers to move money, hold the transfer and alert the fraud team.
options.outcome: A customer moving savings while a caller gives instructions is a classic fraud sign. Respecting his choice does not mean ignoring clear warning signs; pause and ask gentle questions first.

options.text: Process the Birr 250,000 transfer: it is his money, he gives clear instructions, and refusing a competent adult customer is not our decision.
options.outcome: Right. Spot it, talk to him, own it and pass it up. Once the caller is gone, he can think calmly, and the fraud team can act on the receiving account.

options.text: Take the phone and ask the caller for his staff number and department, then check it with head office before deciding on the transfer.
options.outcome: A fraudster will happily give a fake staff number. The safe move is to end the call and speak to the customer alone; the bank never asks customers to move money.

options.text: Refuse the transfer today and ask him to come back tomorrow with his son, so a family member can confirm the transfer is genuine.
options.outcome: The money is protected today, but refusing without explaining leaves him confused, and needing a relative to decide for him is not fair treatment. Explain the fraud, and let him decide once he understands.

tasks.subject: Visually impaired customer wants a savings account
body: Weizero Genet Alemu, a telephone operator who is visually impaired, wants to open a savings account for her salary. She came alone with a valid Fayda ID. The officer tells her she must come back with a relative who can read the form and sign for her.
tasks.ask: What do you tell the officer?

options.text: Open it today: read the form aloud, take her thumbprint or signature before a witness and an officer, fix her photo, and note supervisor authorization.
options.outcome: Right. Fair treatment means changing the support, not the rules. She opens the account in her own name today, and the procedure protects her and the bank.

options.text: Agree with the officer: ask her to come back with a relative who can read the form, check the terms and sign for her, so she is fully protected.
options.outcome: An adult customer opens her own account. Making her depend on a relative is unfair, may breach the rights of persons with disabilities and puts her money at risk from others.

options.text: Open it now with her thumbprint while the hall is busy, and have a colleague add the witness signature this afternoon when things are quieter.
options.outcome: The witness must be present when the thumbprint is taken. A witness who signs afterwards witnessed nothing, and the file is defective.

options.text: Suggest she use mobile banking instead, with the app's voice reader, so she can manage her salary without visiting the branch or filling in forms.
options.outcome: Mobile banking may help her later, but it still needs an account, and deciding for her what she can use is not fair treatment. Offer help and let her choose.

tasks.subject: "Did my loan come out?"
body: Weizero Bethlehem asks loudly at the counter about her Birr 300,000 business loan. The credit team declined it this morning: her existing loan installments at another bank already take most of her monthly income. Last week a relationship manager told her it "would surely be approved", and she has already ordered stock.
Twelve people in the queue can hear.

options.text: Take her to a private desk, give the decision and reason plainly, discuss next steps, record it, and report the RM's promise.
options.outcome: Right. Privacy, a clear reason and a way forward keep her dignity and the relationship. The RM's promise must be raised: staff never promise approval before the assessment.

options.text: Tell her at the counter that the credit team declined the application because of her existing loans, so she hears the reason straight away.
options.outcome: True, but delivered in front of twelve people and with no reason or next step. A loan decline is a conversation for a private desk.

options.text: Show her the credit team's assessment sheet, so she can see the numbers herself and understand that the decision was not yours.
options.outcome: Internal assessments and scores are not shared. Explain the main reason in plain words, without blaming the credit team or the system.

options.text: Tell her the file is still with the credit team and ask her to come back next week, so the news can be given when the hall is quieter.
options.outcome: An untrue excuse only delays the bad news and costs her another week of stock costs. Honest, private and clear is kinder.

tasks.subject: Third visit: Birr 12,000 left my account and never arrived
body: Weizero Rahel sent Birr 12,000 by mobile banking to her sister's account at another bank last Friday. Her account was debited; her sister has received nothing. This is her third visit, and nobody has recorded a complaint yet. Today is Thursday 5 November, and there are no public holidays in the next month.
You check the system.

exhibit.title: Transaction status and Bank A's complaint timeline (example procedure)

rows.label: Transfer status
rows.value: Sent to the national switch; rejected by the receiving bank: account number not found

tasks.ask: What do you do and promise?

options.text: Log a complaint with a reference, explain the wrong account number and pending reversal, follow up in 2 days; final reply by 26 November.
options.outcome: Right. Fifteen working days from Thursday 5 November, with no holidays, ends on Thursday 26 November, but a simple reversal should be settled well before. Show her how to check the payee name before confirming, the fix that cut transfer complaints in the course.

options.text: Credit Birr 12,000 back from branch funds now, since this is her third visit and the reversal is already initiated, and clear it when it arrives.
options.outcome: Crediting without completing the investigation breaks controls, and when the reversal arrives she is credited twice. Record, follow the reversal and keep her informed.

options.text: Explain that the receiving bank rejected the transfer, so the delay is on its side, and give her its customer service number to follow up.
options.outcome: The money is in Bank A's reversal process, so it is Bank A's job to follow up. A complaint is received and recorded wherever it starts.

options.text: Record the complaint with a reference and tell her the final reply under the procedure will come no later than Monday 30 November.
options.outcome: Recording it is right, but the date is wrong and too slow: 15 working days from Thursday 5 November is Thursday 26 November, and a simple case should be resolved within 2 working days.

tasks.subject: Shouting in the hall: "Your ATM stole my money"
body: Ato Mesfin shouts at window 3 that the ATM outside debited Birr 4,000 but gave him no cash, and that he needs the money tonight for his mother's medicine. He says the bank is full of thieves and demands the manager. Twenty people are watching. He is angry but not threatening.

options.text: Bring him to my desk, hear him out, apologize, log the ATM dispute with a reference, and help him with a counter withdrawal for tonight.
options.outcome: Security is for threats, not for anger. Removing an upset customer with a real problem makes it worse and twenty people see it.

options.text: Call security to escort him out calmly, so the twenty customers waiting can be served and the hall is not disturbed by his shouting.
options.outcome: HEARD in practice: hear, empathize, apologize, resolve the next step, diagnose later. Moving him away from the audience lowers the tension, and the counter withdrawal meets his need while the ATM journal is checked.

options.text: Pay him Birr 4,000 from the till now, since his need is urgent and the ATM probably failed, and reconcile the ATM journal tomorrow.
options.outcome: Paying out before the ATM is reconciled breaks cash controls and leaves the till short. Record the dispute and follow the procedure; a counter withdrawal from his own balance meets tonight's need.

options.text: Explain firmly that ATM disputes need an investigation of the machine journal, and that he must wait for the result before any refund.
options.outcome: Correct about the investigation, but he has not been heard and his urgent need is unmet. Feelings first, then the facts.

followUps.from: Weizero Aster Tefera and her son, by phone from Toronto
followUps.subject: "My mother never received the money"
body: Weizero Aster's son calls: his mother says she never received the Birr 75,000; the nephew kept it. He wants to know how the bank paid someone who was not the recipient, and he is thinking of using another bank.

options.text: Log the complaint, escalate to the branch manager, review the voucher and CCTV, explain honestly, and offer her an account in her own name.
options.outcome: The right recovery: own the error, investigate and keep the family informed. The lesson stands: remittances are paid only to the named recipient, whoever is standing next to her.

options.text: Explain that his mother agreed at the counter in front of the teller, the voucher is countersigned, and the bank therefore considers the matter closed.
options.outcome: Her quiet agreement under pressure does not change the rule the bank broke. Closing the matter loses the family and invites a complaint to the NBE.

options.text: Promise him the bank will refund the full Birr 75,000 to his mother today, to keep the family's remittances coming to Bank A.
options.outcome: You cannot promise an outcome before the investigation and the branch manager's decision. Promise a reference, an investigation and a date, then keep it.

followUps.subject: My father's Birr 250,000 is gone
body: Ato Worku's son arrives with his father. The "head office" caller has stopped answering, and the receiving account was emptied within an hour of yesterday's transfer. They ask what the bank can still do.

options.text: Report the receiving account via the fraud channel, log the complaint, tell the manager, and explain recovery is not certain.
options.outcome: Speed and honesty are what the bank can offer now. The lesson stands: when a caller is giving a customer instructions, end the call and talk to the customer first.

options.text: Explain that Ato Worku authorized the transfer himself at the counter, so the bank followed his instruction and cannot reverse it.
options.outcome: Even after an authorized transfer, the bank can report and trace the receiving account. Refusing to try fails a vulnerable customer.

options.text: Promise the family the full Birr 250,000 will be recovered within a week, since the receiving account details are on record.
options.outcome: Never promise a time or result you cannot control. Recovery depends on the receiving account holder and bank; say so honestly.

memo.prompt: Write your end-of-week hand-over note to the branch manager, Ato Fikadu Tessema.
guide: The two customer moments you handled best this week, and the rule or skill behind each.
Open complaints with their reference numbers and the dates you have promised a reply.
Any staff practice you want to correct (breaks at peak, promises on loans or rates, products opened the wrong way) and how you will coach it.
One change to the hall or the journey that would cut queues or repeat visits next month.

exam.q: Kera branch receives 120 customers an hour at peak. Each teller takes 5 minutes per customer. How many windows must be open to stop the queue growing?
exam.explain: One teller serves 12 per hour (60 / 5); 120 / 12 = 10 windows.

exam.q: With 4 windows open and service time of 4 minutes, 75 customers arrive each hour. How many are waiting after 2 hours, if none were waiting at the start?
exam.explain: Capacity is 60 per hour, so the queue grows by 15 each hour: 30 after 2 hours.

exam.q: Which statement about deposit rates since January 2026 is correct?
options: The NBE sets a 7% minimum savings rate
Rates are set by the branch
Each bank's board sets rates on written criteria and reports them to the NBE
Interest-free accounts must pay the same rate
exam.explain: NBE/INT/13/2026 lets banks set rates freely, with board approval and reporting.

exam.q: A trader's wallet already holds Birr 60,000. He expects Birr 25,000 more today. Under ONPS/09/2023, what is the best advice?
options: Receive the payment into a linked bank account, since the wallet balance limit is Birr 75,000
No problem, the limit is Birr 150,000
Open a second wallet in his wife's name
Ask payers to wait until tomorrow
exam.explain: Birr 85,000 would exceed the Birr 75,000 balance limit; the Birr 150,000 figure is the daily transaction limit.

exam.q: A customer places Birr 120,000 in a fixed deposit for 6 months at an illustrative 10% a year and withdraws after 2 months. What is the most likely outcome to explain?
options: She gets Birr 6,000 interest
She pays a penalty equal to the deposit
The bank must refuse the withdrawal
Interest is lost or reduced under the early withdrawal terms
exam.explain: Early withdrawal usually loses or reduces interest; this must be explained before she signs.

exam.q: A customer asks for an interest-free product. Which is correct under SBB/72/2019?
options: Open a conventional savings account and do not pay interest
Open an interest-free product kept separate from conventional business
Interest-free banking is only for full-fledged interest-free banks
Refer the customer to a microfinance institution
exam.explain: The directive allows interest-free windows and banks, with the business kept separate.

exam.q: A Birr 50,000 one-year loan at 18% has a 2% fee deducted at the start, with interest repaid at the end. What is the APR, approximately?
A lender offers Birr 60,000 over 12 months at 15% flat. What is the monthly installment?
options: Birr 5,000
Birr 5,415
Birr 5,750
Birr 6,000

exam.q: Which response best explains a loan decline?
options: 'The system rejected you.'
'The credit team did not like your file.'
'The bank cannot approve this amount because your current repayments already take most of your income; a smaller amount or repaying the existing loan first could change that.'
'Try another bank.'
exam.explain: It gives the decision, the main reason in plain words and a next step, without blaming anyone.

exam.q: A low-literacy customer has listened to the terms of a savings account. What is the best check of understanding?
options: Ask 'Is everything clear?'
Ask her to explain in her own words what the fee is and when she can withdraw
Ask her to sign quickly
Give her the brochure to take home
exam.explain: Teach-back reveals gaps that a yes or no question hides.

exam.q: A woman from a rural area wants to open an account alone. A colleague insists her husband must sign. What principle is at stake?
options: KYC
Data protection
Interest-free banking
Non-discrimination and fair treatment
exam.explain: Requiring a husband for her own account treats her unfairly because of her gender.

exam.q: A remittance recipient has an expired kebele ID, and the names and reference match. What should the teller do?
options: Ask for a valid, unexpired ID before paying, and explain the money is safe
Pay, since the details match
Pay half
Return the money to the operator
exam.explain: An expired ID is not valid verification under the bank's KYC procedure.

exam.q: Expected till cash is Birr 520,000. Counted cash is Birr 519,300. A Birr 200 counterfeit was retained from a deposit and only genuine notes were credited. What is the position?
options: Birr 700 short, of which the counterfeit explains Birr 200
Balanced
Birr 700 short, none of it explained by the counterfeit, to be reported at once
Birr 500 short
exam.explain: Only genuine notes were credited, so the counterfeit is not part of the expected cash; the full Birr 700 shortage must be reported.

exam.q: Which is an example of data protection good practice at the counter?
options: Turning screens away from the queue and confirming details only to verified customers
Writing customer phone numbers on a notepad by the window
Sharing account details with family members who know the account number
Sending ID copies through a personal phone
exam.explain: Limit access to customer data and disclose only to authorized people.

exam.q: An elderly customer withdraws Birr 150,000 while someone on the phone tells him what to say. He has never withdrawn more than Birr 10,000. What should staff do?
options: Pay quickly to avoid a scene
Refuse and close his account
Ask the caller to come to the branch
Pause, gently ask about the purpose, ask him to end the call and involve the supervisor
exam.explain: These are classic fraud signs; pause and escalate while protecting the customer.

exam.q: A complaint is acknowledged on a Wednesday. Under Bank A's example procedure, the final reply is due within 15 working days. When is the deadline, if no public holidays fall in the period?
options: The Wednesday two weeks later
The Wednesday three weeks later
The Thursday three weeks later
The Friday four weeks later
exam.explain: Fifteen working days are three full working weeks, so the deadline is the Wednesday three weeks later.

exam.q: A complaint has been resolved at head office, but no one has told the customer. What is its status?
options: Closed
Escalated
Open until the customer is told the outcome and reason
Withdrawn
exam.explain: A complaint closes only after the customer receives the response.

exam.q: A customer shouts at the counter in front of the queue. Which first step is best?
options: Raise your voice so you are heard
Invite him to a desk, let him speak fully and acknowledge his frustration
Call security
Ask him to put the complaint in writing
exam.explain: Moving away from the audience and hearing him out lowers the tension; security is for threats.

exam.q: A role play scores 5, 5, 2, 5, 5 out of 5 on weights 10%, 20%, 30%, 20%, 20%, with no compliance breach. What is the percentage, and does it pass at 70%?
options: 82%, pass
74%, pass
64%, fail
90%, pass

exam.q: In the same role play, the learner had told a caller a customer's approximate balance. What is the result?
options: Pass at 82%
Pass with a warning
Repeat only the compliance part
Fail, because the compliance gate overrides the score
exam.explain: A disclosure to an unverified third party is a compliance breach, which fails the role play.
